What's an access code?

Each user has their own code. It identifies your library and lets it sync between devices. If you don't have one yet, ask the person who invited you for an invite link or code.

If you've lost your code, contact your admin to issue you a new one. Codes are not recoverable through this app.

Supported URLs:

  • 🎮 Games (IGDB): igdb.com/games/<slug>
  • 🎮 Games (RAWG): rawg.io/games/<slug>
  • 📚 Books: openlibrary.org/works/OLxxxxW
  • 💿 Albums: musicbrainz.org/release-group/<uuid>

Each media-type group (Games / Movies / TV / Books / Albums) within Backlog, In Progress, and Completed will show up to this many cards initially. Click "Show more" to reveal more in chunks of the same size.

Displays a small "via OMDb / IGDB / Jikan…" tag on each card so you can see where its metadata came from. Helpful when comparing sources.

When adding a title, query every available source at once and merge the results into one picker — each labeled by source, with the best match starred. Currently games search both IGDB and RAWG. Turn off to use a single source per type.

Toggle and reorder sections on your home screen.

Highlight backlog items untouched for 1+ year with a "Still interested?" nudge. Helps keep your backlog fresh and honest.

With "Compare across sources" on, the picker queries OMDb and TMDb together and merges results. This setting controls which one leads when comparing is off. The picker also has a "switch source" button to flip to Jikan for anime mid-add.

IGDB setup — credentials live as Netlify environment variables.
  1. Sign in at dev.twitch.tv/console, register an application (OAuth Redirect: http://localhost, category: Application Integration)
  2. Copy the Client ID; click "New Secret" for a Client Secret
  3. In Netlify: Site configuration → Environment variables → add TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET
  4. Trigger a redeploy
Free tier: 60,000 requests/month.
RAWG setup
  1. Get a free key at rawg.io/apidocs
  2. In Netlify: add env var RAWG_API_KEY
  3. Trigger a redeploy
Free tier: 20,000 requests/month.
OMDb setup — gives Rotten Tomatoes scores for movies, IMDb ratings for both.
  1. Get a free key at omdbapi.com/apikey.aspx (1,000 requests/day on free tier; $1/mo for unlimited)
  2. In Netlify: add env var OMDB_API_KEY
  3. Trigger a redeploy
Note: OMDb only returns Rotten Tomatoes scores for movies. TV shows get IMDb rating instead.
Open Library setup — no signup, no API key needed.

Open Library is a free service from the Internet Archive. Returns title, author, year, page count, cover art, and rough genre tags. Just works once you select it.

MusicBrainz setup — no signup, no API key needed.

MusicBrainz is the gold-standard open music database. Returns artist, year, album type, and the full track listing. Cover art via the sister Cover Art Archive. Rate-limited to 1 request/sec, so back-to-back additions of many albums may pause briefly.

Claude API setup

Stored only on this device. Get a key at console.anthropic.com. Costs a fraction of a cent per item added. Works without any server setup.

Add your own genres alongside the built-in ones. They'll appear in the genre dropdown when editing cards and in the filter chips.

The app keeps automatic point-in-time snapshots of your library — locally, and (when signed in) a copy in the cloud kept separate from live sync. If anything ever goes wrong, restore a known-good snapshot here. Restoring first snapshots your current state, so it's always reversible.

Get gentle reminders even when you haven't opened the app — like "you haven't updated your in-progress items in a while" or "your backlog is getting big." Notifications check once per day and never send more than one per day.

The admin can see aggregate stats about your library — total entry count, breakdown by media type (e.g., "12 games, 4 movies"), and your top genres.

The admin cannot see your specific titles, ratings, notes, or anything else about individual entries.
